issues.description: The PersonResource constructor in the solution repository has an incorrect parameter type (String) instead of the expected PersonService. This creates a constructor-parameter type mismatch: the field personService is of type PersonService but the constructor accepts a String, causing the solution code to be uncompilable and contradicting the template's correct constructor signature. Students comparing template and solution could be confused and the provided solution would not build or run.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the constructor parameter in solution_repository/src/main/java/de/tum/in/ase/eist/rest/PersonResource.java from String to PersonService (i.e., public PersonResource(PersonService personService) { this.personService = personService; }). Ensure the constructor parameter type matches the personService field type so the class compiles and aligns with the template and intended design.

issues.description: Constructor parameter type for PersonResource differs between template and solution. The template defines PersonResource(PersonService personService) while the solution defines PersonResource(String personService). This mismatched identifier/type for the same conceptual dependency (PersonService) creates confusion and will prevent students from mapping the REST controller to its service dependency and causes a compile-time/type error in the solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the constructor in the solution to accept a PersonService parameter to match the template and the conceptual dependency: public PersonResource(PersonService personService) { this.personService = personService; }
